messages:
Olivia (Support): FYI — customer_acct_42 is seeing intermittent 510s when sending large batch embeddings to the hosted API. Ticket #45321. They say it started ~today after a spike in batch size. Repro steps attached below.

customer_acct_42: seeing ~10% of requests return 510, usually on jobs with batch_size >= 512. SDK retries keep looping but eventually give up. No changes on our side that they know of.

Olivia (Support): Repro with curl and SDK snippet incoming. Asking for eng help /eng-runtime /eng-sre — low severity but customer hitting production traffic.

Raj (eng-runtime): looking. Can you paste the exact curl or SDK payload that repros? Also need request_id from logs if you have one.

Olivia (Support): here's sanitized payload from customer (they anonymized texts).

```
POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer ***
Content-Type: application/json

{ "model": "embed-ld-002", "input": ["...large array ~512 items..."] }
```

Olivia (Support): customer says response header shows `x-request-id: rq_17aBcD` for one failing call. Log snippet from their side: `HTTP/1.1 510` with empty body.

Ada (oncall): pinging eng-sre, will try to reproduce from our side. Any quick rate-limit or quota hits? 510 isn't a typical rate-limit code.

Tom (eng-sre): I can repro locally against prod edge in staging — when body > ~1.8MB the edge responds 510, smaller payloads 200. Looks like an upstream rejection. Dumping proxy logs now.

Tom (eng-sre): proxy log entry for rq_17aBcD:
```
[edge-proxy] 2026-03-15T15:22:10Z rq_17aBcD client_ip=34.72.10.5 method=POST path=/v1/embeddings status=510 bytes=0 upstream="upstream-embed-01" note="upstream reset"
```

Raj (eng-runtime): hmm. Could be client_body_buffer_size overflow or WAF rule triggered by payload fingerprinting. Did the customer send any base64 attachments?

customer_acct_42: no attachments, just long plain strings (product descriptions). We used the SDK default `batch_size=512` and `concurrency=4`.

Maya (Product): we should check if a recent routing change touched the edge config. Raj, any recent deploys touching gateway?

Raj (eng-runtime): there was a small nginx config bump last week but nothing touching buffer sizes. I'll try reproducing from our env with the exact payload.

Olivia (Support): customer is on a tight timeline; they asked if we have a temporary workaround they can use now while you debug.

Raj (eng-runtime): short-term: reduce `batch_size` to 256 or stream smaller sub-batches. I'll also add an SDK advisory to recommend smaller batches for now. Long-term we need to find root cause.

Ada (oncall): running an automated curl to reproduce:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
```

Ada (oncall): got 510 consistently with test payload > 1.8MB. When I split the payload into two calls (~900KB each) both returned 200. So it's payload-size correlated.

Tom (eng-sre): digging into edge pool: upstream-embed-01 reported `connection reset by peer` around same timeframe. Could be the embedding service itself closing connection if it can't allocate memory for large batches. Checking upstream logs.

Raj (eng-runtime): good call. If the runtime process OOMs on large KV cache allocation, it might reset. Any OOM traces?

Tom (eng-sre): found an OOM-kill event on embed-worker-3 at 15:21:59Z. Kernel log: `oom_killer invoked pid=8421` and process `embed-worker` exited. That matches the 510 window.

Maya (Product): so not an edge buffer after all; embedding workers are being killed by OOM when handling large batches. That explains why splitting avoids the issue.

Olivia (Support): relaying to customer: recommend reducing batch_size to 256 for now and we will follow up with a fix. Would you like me to send a suggested patch for them to try?

customer_acct_42: yes please — they prefer an SDK config change they can apply quickly.

Raj (eng-runtime): immediate mitigation: bump worker memory limit on embed-worker deployments and add a defensive check in runtime to reject single-request allocations that would exceed available memory (return 413 or a clear error instead of letting OOM kill the process). I'll open an internal PR.

Tom (eng-sre): incrementing embed-worker mem limit in staging and will canary to prod in 15m. Also adding alert if OOM rate >0 in 5m window.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: embed-worker-memory-bump to prod at 2026-03-15T15:40:00Z (rolling, 10% batch). CI: green.

inc-bot: incident created — INC-2026-0315-embed-oom — Sev3 — assigned to eng-runtime and eng-sre.

Raj (eng-runtime): PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/982 (defensive allocation + clearer 4xx response). Will land after tests.

Tom (eng-sre): prod canary looks good so far (10%): no OOMs in canary cluster. Starting remainder of rollout.

Olivia (Support): customer updated: told them to set `batch_size=256` and we'll notify when fix fully rolled out. They said that work-around is fine for now.

Eve (Billing): quick check — no billing impact expected. These 510s are not chargeable retries; we'll ensure retries don't double-bill.

Ada (oncall): full rollout finished at 15:48Z. Post-deploy checks: no OOMs in last 30m and no 510 spikes for test traffic.

Raj (eng-runtime): PR merged and config rolled; added unit + integ tests to assert we return `413 Payload Too Large` if the requested batch allocation would exceed threshold. Also added metrics `runtime.request_alloc_bytes` to monitor.

Olivia (Support): closing loop with customer: deployment done, recommended `batch_size=256` as permanent best practice for now while we optimize memory path. Customer confirmed they see 200s on previous failing jobs after retrying. :tada:

customer_acct_42: thanks all — appreciate quick turnaround.

Maya (Product): action items: 1) Docs update for embeddings batch sizing, 2) SDK advisory for default max_batch_size 256, 3) longer-term memory optimizations for embed worker. I'll track in PG-118.

Olivia (Support): marking ticket #45321 as resolved pending retrospective. Will follow up with a short postmortem in #postmortems.

Tom (eng-sre): NOTE for postmortem: root cause = lack of defensive allocation check + conservative worker memory limits; symptom = OOM -> connection reset -> edge surfaces 510. Mitigation = memory bump + 413 defensive response + SDK docs.

Raj (eng-runtime): adding monitoring dashboards and alert runbook to ensure quick detection next time.

Olivia (Support): thanks team. Closing thread.
